headline: From AI Image to Interactive World: A Four-Tool Solo Pipeline
lede: Ian Curtis — who posts as @XRarchitect and works as a product designer at World Labs — demonstrated a pipeline that converts a single AI-generated panorama into a navigable, photorealistic 3-D environment. The subject was deliberately playful: a Golden State Warriors-themed spaceship interior, rendered in gold and blue. The technique is not: it suggests the gap between a text prompt and an interactive 3-D world has narrowed to four tools and a browser.
body:
The pipeline begins with **ChatGPT Images 2.0** — OpenAI's image-generation model released in late April 2026, which can produce *equirectangular* 360° panoramas through careful prompting. An equirectangular image maps a full spherical view — 360° horizontal, 180° vertical — onto a flat 2:1 rectangle, the format used by VR headsets and photosphere apps. Prompt for it correctly and the output wraps seamlessly around the inside of a virtual sphere. On its own, though, the result is a glorified *photosphere*: visually rich, spatially flat, with no parallax as the viewer moves.

That flatness is what **Marble**, from World Labs, resolves. Marble ingests a panoramic image and runs it through a generative *world model* — an AI system trained on enough 3-D scene data to infer spatial depth and fill in the geometry hidden behind visible surfaces. Within roughly 30 seconds, the upload produces a *Gaussian splat* scene. Gaussian splatting, introduced in a 2023 paper by researchers at the French national institute INRIA, represents a 3-D scene as millions of semi-transparent ellipsoids — each with position, color, and opacity — rendered at over 100 frames per second on consumer hardware. The result looks photorealistic from any angle, with genuine spatial extent rather than a texture painted on a sphere.

The splat scene travels from Marble to the browser via **Spark**, World Labs' open-source Gaussian splatting renderer for Three.js, the most widely used *WebGL* 3-D library on the web. Spark loads the splat as a first-class Three.js object, letting it sit beside conventional geometry and be post-processed like any other render target. Curtis layers two effects on top: *depth of field* (DoF), which blurs objects outside the camera's focal plane in the manner of a real lens and sharpens the sense of physical depth; and splat particle effects, where individual Gaussian splats are repurposed as procedural visual flourishes — ambient haze, stylized bursts — rather than locked-in scene reconstruction.

The workflow is arguably as much product showcase as creative experiment. World Labs — founded by Fei-Fei Li, the Stanford computer scientist and AI pioneer — shipped Marble in late 2025, and Curtis joined the company that October as a product designer and member of technical staff. The complete toolchain from image prompt to walkable, post-processed world is now essentially a World Labs stack with a single open-source dependency. Whether that makes immersive creation genuinely democratic, or simply shifts the bottleneck from technical skill to aesthetic judgment, remains an open question — but the distance between a text prompt and a room you can walk around in has rarely looked shorter.

concepts.definition: A standard mapping format that unwraps a full 360°×180° spherical view onto a flat 2:1 rectangle. It is the format used by photosphere apps, VR headsets, and most 360° cameras. When displayed, the image is re-mapped onto the inside of a virtual sphere so the viewer sees a seamless panorama in every direction.

A 360° photograph mapped onto the inside surface of a virtual sphere, allowing the viewer to look in any direction. Unlike a true 3-D environment, a photosphere has no depth: moving the camera forward or sideways produces no parallax, so the illusion of space collapses quickly under movement.

A technique for representing and rendering 3-D scenes as millions of semi-transparent ellipsoids called Gaussian splats. Each splat stores position, orientation, scale, opacity, and view-dependent color. Because splats are rasterized on a GPU rather than queried through a neural network, the technique achieves over 100 frames per second on consumer hardware — far faster than earlier neural approaches such as NeRF.

An AI system trained to understand and predict the spatial structure of 3-D environments, not merely their pixel appearance. World Labs' version ingests flat 2-D images and infers depth, hidden geometry, and scene layout — enabling reconstruction of a navigable 3-D space from a single photograph or panorama.

A post-processing effect that simulates how a physical camera lens works: objects at a chosen focal distance appear sharp, while objects nearer or farther progressively blur (the out-of-focus quality is called bokeh). In 3-D rendering, DoF is computed after the main render pass using depth-buffer data, and it dramatically increases the sense that a scene occupies real space.

A browser API that gives JavaScript direct access to the device's graphics processing unit (GPU), enabling real-time 3-D rendering without a plugin. Three.js is the dominant JavaScript library built on top of WebGL, abstracting its low-level complexity — shader programs, vertex buffers, texture units — into a higher-level scene-graph API.

repos.summary: Spark is World Labs' open-source Gaussian splatting renderer for Three.js, written in TypeScript and Rust compiled to WebAssembly. It loads standard splat formats (.PLY, .SPZ, .RAD) as first-class Three.js objects, enabling real-time splat rendering alongside conventional geometry in a browser. Version 2.0 (April 2026) added continuous level-of-detail streaming and GPU virtual memory paging, making scenes of 100 million or more splats practical on consumer devices.

Three.js is the most widely used JavaScript library for GPU-accelerated 3-D graphics in web browsers, built on top of WebGL. It provides a scene-graph abstraction over raw WebGL — cameras, lights, geometries, materials, and a post-processing pipeline — and supports the WebXR Device API for VR and AR headsets. With over 2,000 contributors and an MIT license, it is the de facto standard for browser-based interactive 3-D.

fact_check: Two clarifications worth flagging. First, generating 360° equirectangular images from ChatGPT Images 2.0 requires specific prompt engineering (specifying 'equirectangular' and a 2:1 aspect ratio); it is not a dedicated mode or built-in toggle. Second, 'Spark' in this context is World Labs' Gaussian splatting renderer for Three.js — not Meta Spark AR, Meta's creator platform for Instagram effects, which shut down permanently in January 2025.
